rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for someone or something wilful, capricious, or difficult to control.

example.english: That child is very wayward and refuses to eat whenever he dislikes the food.

rows.note: Use this when “wayward” mainly stresses obstinacy or refusal to change, rather than straying from expectations.

example.english: You are so wayward that you refuse to change no matter how much everyone advises you.

rows.note: Use this when someone deliberately follows their own way and ignores the expected norm.

example.english: They have always been wayward, doing whatever they want and ignoring what other people think.
